### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 73155fedcacc215565c4eef6d9899977e0707010` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `262804cfd94548466e8794783360042b5a27d024` — the merge of head `2b8df02e7aca4b62cbf44ea8860d6f8a638916aa` into base `73155fedcacc215565c4eef6d9899977e0707010`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 262804cfd94548466e8794783360042b5a27d024 && git checkout 262804cfd94548466e8794783360042b5a27d024
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 73155fedcacc215565c4eef6d9899977e0707010 2b8df02e7aca4b62cbf44ea8860d6f8a638916aa && git checkout -B drift-repro 73155fedcacc215565c4eef6d9899977e0707010 && git merge --no-ff 2b8df02e7aca4b62cbf44ea8860d6f8a638916aa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 73155fedcacc215565c4eef6d9899977e0707010
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b8df02e7aca4b62cbf44ea8860d6f8a638916aa`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20730 body and its five comments (`5901102672`, `5901360064`, `5904663679`, `5906742753`, `5908785750`); PR #20832 body and file list; the net diff `git diff 261c529f0 refs/review/pr-20832` (merge-base against `origin/main`, 5 files, +474/-16, the same five paths the file list and the dev report name); the check-runs on the head, collapsed latest-per-name; at the merge-base `261c529f0`: `getPackagedObjectBase`, `getPackagedDashboardBase`, `getPackagedViewBase` and `lookupArtifactItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`), `TranslateDocumentOptions.packagedBase`, `translateDashboard`, `translateView`, `translateGlobalFilter`, `valueOverridesPackagedBase` and the translator dispatch table (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`), the pre-state of `translateMetaList` / `translateMetaDocument` / `packagedObjectBaseOf`, both transports' `resolveProtocol` (`rest-server.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`), `expandViewContainer` and the engine's view registration, ADR-0126's tier table and ADR-0029 D9.2a, `check-engine-double-contract.mjs` and its pinned ledger, `clause2-line.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-doc-authoring.mjs` ROOTS, and the pm-dispatch filing gate. Governed surfaces: none of the five paths is one (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success).

Check-runs on the head, converged (the one run still `in_progress` when the brief was written, `Lint & Repo Gates`, completed `success` at 2026-09-30T10:21:01Z; polled in the background until every run completed): 35 names, all on `2b8df02e7`, 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, path-filtered with no `.objectui-sha` change; `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failed. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on; nothing was built, run or re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The resolver — one table, three accessors, both callers.** RIGHT.

- `packagedObjectBaseOf` now reads `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS`, a module-private `ReadonlyMap` of `object` to `getPackagedObjectBase`, `dashboard` to `getPackagedDashboardBase`, `view` to `getPackagedViewBase`. Each row hands the translator the base its own rule compares against: `object` is unchanged (the owner's pre-fold declaration, what `translateObject` compares — ADR-0029 D9.2a); `dashboard` is `lookupArtifactItem('dashboard', name)`, the packaged body keyed by the dashboard name, which is the key the catalog (`dashboards.NAME.widgets.ID.title`) and `translateDashboard` both use; `view` is `lookupArtifactItem('view', name)` keyed by the served item's registry name. That name IS the qualified `OBJECT.VIEW_KEY`: `expandViewContainer` names each expanded item `${object}.${key}` and the engine registers every one under it, the item read passes `document.name` and the list read passes each element's `item.name`, and the accessor's own docblock demands exactly that name and refuses the bare key. `lookupArtifactItem` prefers the composite `packageId:name` entry, so the base handed over is the packaged body and never the overlay hydrated under the plain key — the comparison runs against the right side.
- Unknown type: `Map.get` answers `undefined` and the function returns before it reads the name or the protocol — the same early exit the old `type !== 'object'` guard gave, and a `Map` rather than an object literal, so `toString` / `constructor` cannot resolve to an accessor (§1 pin). Empty name, a protocol without the accessor and a throwing accessor still answer `undefined`, the edges unchanged.
- Both callers gate on the same table: `translateMetaList` resolves the protocol once per page when `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS.has(metaType)`, `translateMetaDocument` the same per document, and both hand the result through `packagedObjectBaseOf`, which re-gates. So every type in the table and nothing else — of the seven translatable types, `action`, `app`, `dataset`, `page` get no protocol resolution and no base, exactly as before. Both transports already hand `resolveProtocol` unconditionally (`RestServer.metaItemTranslationSources` / `metaListTranslationSources`, and the runtime's `metaTranslationSources` returns the `MetaDomainProtocol` it was given), so no transport edit was needed and none was made; `rest-server.ts` is untouched as the claim's stop line demanded.
- One consequence read and found harmless: on a `view` list the container element the boot registers under the bare object name now also reaches `getPackagedViewBase`, which answers the container; `translateView` compares its absent `label` and `valueOverridesPackagedBase` answers false for a non-string value, so that element translates exactly as before.

**(b) The behaviour the card asks for.** RIGHT, each claim pinned; nothing served differently for a caller or type the card did not name.

- `meta-dashboard-view-i18n-explicit-override.test.ts` (52 tests) runs the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over a real `SchemaRegistry` through the registered `/meta` routes, registering the packaged items the way the engine does (dashboard by name; the view container under the bare object name AND each expanded item under `OBJECT.VIEW_KEY`) and seeding the overlay as the published org row (`package_id: null`, the org, `state: 'active'`); the 14th constructor argument is `i18nServiceProvider`, verified against the constructor at the merge-base.
- §2 dashboard and §3 view each cover the eight cells — item and list read, admin and member of one org, `en` and `zh-CN` — three times: the edited widget / view serves the edit; the unedited widget (`widget_organizations`) / the unedited view (`showcase_task.urgent`) stays translated; with no overlay row (the state after a reset) the shipped string is served, translated. The `en` cell matters: the bundle's `en` repeats the shipped string, which is the shape `platform-objects` ships and the shape that made an `en` reader lose the edit. The showcase control (a dashboard whose catalog carries only a label) serves an overlay edit on both reads with its label still translated. The object path: its accessor row is byte-unchanged and the PR's ablation of the resolver to object-only leaves the object suite green.
- The card's pins from triage `5901360064` and pointer `5904663679` are each one of those cells. The reset pin is served at the read boundary by absence of the row; the write verb itself is not driven in the pin, and the PR's real-boot probe (`DELETE` answering 200, 0 served diffs in the reset phase) covers that leg.
- Reach beyond the card: none. The only new served behaviour is on `dashboard` and `view`, both named by the card; the probe's 12 changed leaf fields are all in the overlaid phase on the two overlaid items (8 dashboard cells; 4 view cells in `zh-CN`, `en` having served the edit already), with 0 diffs on the control, every other dashboard and view, and the app and object lists. The card's 16 came from the parent's probe over a different read set, which the PR says rather than reconciles away.

**(c) Changeset and docs.** RIGHT.

- `.changeset/20730-meta-packaged-base-dashboard-view.md`: `@objectstack/rest: patch`. Every sentence checks against the diff and the merge-base: the four routes named are the item and list doors for the two types; "the translators already let an edited string win when handed the item as the package shipped it, and the metadata protocol already answers that item" is `translateDashboard` / `translateView` plus the two accessors on `main` since `1940afdaf` and `9ad654487` (both ancestors of the merge-base); "the change is in the translation step that both `/meta` transports share" is the two shared functions; "a view is looked up by its full name" is (a). The four consequences are the four pinned cells. "This fixes what the metadata reads serve, not yet what the console draws" scopes the claim to what the diff delivers and states the measured console behaviour at the pin `db11afd4967c` in words. "Nothing to migrate: no key, export or route changed" is true. The body carries no tracker number; the filename's `20730-` prefix is the convention every one of the 120 changesets at the merge-base follows. `Check Changeset` success.
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, new H3 "An edit beats the packaged catalog" under "How a locale is chosen", directly after the sentence about what the REST metadata endpoints serve. Its table was checked string by string against the translators: dashboard `label` / `description`; each widget's `title`, `description` and sub-caption matched by widget `id` (the sub-caption is `options.description` on the document under the bundle key `subCaption`, and the page names it by that key); each global filter's `label` and static option labels matched by the filter key (`name`, else `field`) and the option `value` — all in `translateDashboard` / `translateGlobalFilter`; view `label` / `description`, each bulk action's `label`, `confirmText`, `confirmLabel` and its params' `label`, `help`, `placeholder` matched by `name` — all in `translateView`'s docblock and body. "Dashboards and views are the translated types an organization can edit in place" is ADR-0126 tier A (`view, dashboard, report, translation, email_template`) intersected with the translator table (`view, action, object, app, dashboard, dataset, page`) — exactly those two. "Never shipped counts as edited" is `packagedPart` answering `{}` for a missing part, against which any authored string diverges. The claim is scoped to "the metadata reads serve"; the object rule is stated by reference to `data-modeling/object-extensions`, which exists. No tracker number (the page is inside `check-doc-authoring`'s `content` ROOT). No new page, so `meta.json` owes nothing.
- One observation, not a defect of this diff: the pre-existing sentence just above the new section ("so the Console and any SDUI client get translated metadata without doing lookups themselves") is now measured false for edited strings at the pinned console. It is the objectui defect's prose, and the objectui card's landing is where it gets amended.

**(d) `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`.** RIGHT — exactly the row the gate demands and nothing more. One row added (831 to 832): `packages/rest/src/meta-dashboard-view-i18n-explicit-override.test.ts` / `findOne` / `pinned: 1`, in the ledger's sort position (file, then verb). The test's `findOne` double calls `assertEngineFindOnePredicate(table, q)`, which is the `findOne` slice's `pinCall`; the `find` double has no slice in this gate (the read side is `check-where-matcher-conformance.mjs`), so no second row is owed. The gate's own header says the ledger is written by `--write`, never hand-edited, which is how the row arrived (`8ee4569fa`).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/rest` `patch` and `Clause-②: no` — RIGHT. The Clause-② question (「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, `clause2-line.mjs`) is answered no truthfully: no key is added to any published payload (the served fields are the same fields, now carrying the org's own value where the rule already said they should), no export is added (`PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS` is a module-private `const`), no route, query parameter or write path changes, so no accept set moves. The behaviour change is a defect fix that brings two types under the rule ADR-0029 D9.2a records and the object arm already applied. The line is at line start in the PR body, which is where `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads it (its docblock: "the `Clause-②:` line is a PR body line").

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations (7), each answered:
1. Ledger row outside the claimed surface — accepted; judged in ①(d) as exactly the gate-demanded row.
2. Pin file named beside its object twin — accepted; the new file extends the twin's host shape (RestServer, registered routes, an overridden `resolveExecCtx`) with a real registry and real protocol.
3. `origin/main` merged into the branch (`0a60a2f61`) — accepted; the net diff against the merge-base is the five files and nothing foreign.
4. Stop line held, `rest-server.ts` untouched — accepted and verified in ①(a): both transports already hand the protocol.
5. Changeset and docs scoped to the metadata reads — accepted and verified in ①(c).
6. Heavy runs under `os-verify-lock`, background starts, teardown by recorded pid — procedural, not on the diff; no record item.
7. Cleanup after the report, outcome unreported — procedural; nothing on the head depends on it. The seat may confirm the worktree is gone; not a review matter.

Open questions: none declared, none found.

Out-of-scope findings (3):
1. Class a against objectui — the evidence supports the class and the reach it claims. `reach:` per the filing gate is a public entry with one measured wrong result: the console UI at `/_console/apps/setup/dashboard/system_overview` and `/_console/apps/showcase_app/showcase_task/view/in_progress`, measured in a browser at objectui `db11afd4967c` (this repo's pin) on framework `8ee4569fa`, in `en` and `zh-CN`, drawing the shipped strings while the console's own `/api/v1/meta/dashboard` and `/api/v1/meta/view` responses carry the published edit — the wrong answer is the gap between those two readings, and the pristine and reset phases draw as shipped, so it is the edit that is lost. The dashboard source site is named at the pin (`DashboardRenderer.tsx` `tWidgetTitle`); the view tab and breadcrumb path is declared untraced, so the card's reach is what was drawn, not a source claim for the view half. Dedupe words are supplied. It is the seat's to file in objectui, as triage `5901360064` directed.
2. Stale docblocks (`RestServer.metaItemTranslationSources` / `metaListTranslationSources`, runtime `metaTranslationSources`) still say "object base" — comments only; the behaviour is the shared functions, verified correct. Carrier PR #20683 for `rest-server.ts`; the runtime file has none and rides its next edit. Noted, not filed — right.
3. `packagedObjectBaseOf` keeps its object-only name because `RestServer.packagedObjectBase` (held by PR #20683) calls it — noted, not filed — right; a rename lands with the next edit of that file.
